content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text labels D4 vs C2 as UNDERDETERMINED while relying on the interaction between the Luke 2:48-49 phrases, which is the situation K-S2 governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "In 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand,' I weighed reading (1) a verse with two senses cannot be labeled UNDERDETERMINED because both senses stand against reading (2) one phrase may be qualified by another phrase so the row remains UNDERDETERMINED.", "why": "The judge labels the row UNDERDETERMINED by treating 'thy father' as qualified by 'my Father's business,' contrary to K-S2's command that a verse with two senses is not open and both senses stand."}
